name: TX-37
label: Safe D

key_factors: Casar's large fundraising and cash advantage
model.rationale: The D+30 lean makes this a deep-blue Austin-area seat, and Casar has out-raised Peña roughly ten-to-one while she reports almost no cash on hand. Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 98%, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any sign of a serious Republican outside-spending effort or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-37 covers heavily Democratic Austin, where Greg Casar is seeking another term after winning his first two races by wide margins. The district's D+30 partisan lean alone implies a comfortable Democratic margin even before incumbency advantages. No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing.

Casar has raised about $1.2 million and holds nearly $600,000 on hand, while Republican Lauren Peña has raised roughly $118,000 with under $1,000 remaining and no visible outside support. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 98%. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with low uncertainty given the seat's structural lean and the resource gap.
